Valuation Range

1 · Company Snapshot

Alphabet is a scaled digital platform with one of the highest-quality advertising franchises globally, a growing cloud business, and a balance sheet that gives management unusual strategic flexibility. The investment question is whether AI disruption compresses search economics or reinforces the company's distribution, data, and infrastructure advantages.

1A · Analyst Thesis Overlay

reviewed

Investment Pillars

  • Search and YouTube remain scaled, cash-generative advertising assets.
  • Google Cloud can keep improving margins as utilization and enterprise mix mature.
  • Net cash and buybacks provide downside support while the company invests through the AI transition.

Variant Perception

The market often frames Alphabet as an AI-disruption risk. The variant view is that AI raises capex intensity but also deepens the value of distribution, proprietary data, cloud infrastructure, and advertiser relationships.

Key Debate

Is AI a margin headwind that permanently lowers search monetization, or a product-cycle cost that Alphabet can absorb while defending query share and expanding cloud profitability?

Diligence Questions

  1. How should investors separate temporary AI investment from structural margin pressure?
  2. Which AI products are already improving monetization rather than only engagement?
  3. What is the long-term capital intensity of serving AI-enhanced search results?
  4. How much flexibility does the balance sheet give buybacks if capex remains elevated?
Source: Public demo thesis file.. As of 2026-07-09. Demonstration workflow using public data only; not investment advice.

11 · Methodology Appendix

Forecast. Tier-1 driver model: revenue growth, EBITDA margin, D&A %, capex %, and working-capital glidepaths, anchored on the company's own LTM data; analyst YAML overrides where present (labeled). Taxes at 25% on positive EBIT.

DCF. Mid-year discounting of interim UFCF; terminal value computed both by exit multiple (10.5x EV/EBITDA, analyst assumption) and Gordon perpetuity (3.5% growth), both discounted at year-5; the exit-multiple method is primary. Equity bridge: EV − net debt − minority − preferred; upside measured against market cap (unit-safe), target = current price x (1 + upside).

WACC. CAPM with analyst beta. Every component and fallback listed in section 4.

Assumption provenance. 3 of 3 scenarios analyst-specified (file: GOOGL.yaml); remaining drivers anchored on LTM data. Notes: year-1 growth anchored to NTM consensus (+3.9%); D&A anchor uses the reported TTM field; operating NWC unavailable; using current assets minus current liabilities; AR/inventory/AP days unavailable; NWC projected as % of revenue; terminal ROIC anchored at 10.0%; stable reinvestment equals g / ROIC.
